  "text": "The laundrette had one machine reserved for clothes people died in.

It stood beside the change dispenser, clean as a tooth.

“Cold wash only,” the attendant told me.

I put my sister’s coat inside. There was still a bus ticket in the pocket, but I couldn’t bear to check the date.

“Will it get the blood out?”

“That isn’t what it does.”

She gave me three silver coins.

The machine filled without making a sound.

Through the glass, the coat turned slowly. One sleeve lifted, bent at the elbow, then disappeared beneath the water.

My phone rang.

My sister’s number.

The attendant watched me silence it.

“Good,” she said.

The machine clicked into its next cycle.

My phone rang again.

This time a message followed.

please it’s freezing

I reached for the door handle.

The attendant caught my wrist.

“You open it now, you take home whatever’s wearing it.”

Inside the drum, something pressed against the glass. Five pale fingertips.

“She had a scar,” I said. “On her thumb.”

“They get those right.”

The fingertips stayed there through the spin.

When the machine stopped, the coat lay empty.

I checked both pockets. No ticket. No blood.

At home, I hung it beside my own.

That evening, the laundrette called.

“Did you leave anything in the machine?” the attendant asked.

“Only a bus ticket.”

She was quiet.

Then I heard the shop bell ring at her end.

A familiar voice asked how far it was to my street.

The attendant whispered, “Don’t put your coat on.”"
